who: Historian of ancient and medieval optics, University of Missouri–Columbia.

evidence.says: The 2004 article 'What is the history of medieval optics really about?' identifies A. Mark Smith as professor of history at Missouri–Columbia.
The 2014 publisher biography identifies the optics scholar as Missouri's Curators’ Professor of History and editor/translator of Alhacen's De aspectibus.
Candidate p-8788 records undergraduate history at Glasgow, 2009–2013, and a Glasgow PhD on Pope Leo IX, 2013–2018; this differs from the supervisor's Wisconsin doctorate in 1976.
Candidate p-16329 uses the credit name Andrew W M Smith, records a Queen Mary history PhD completed in 2013, and teaching at UCL and Chichester.
Candidate p-3647 is Andrew D. Smith, Coventry history lecturer and author of British businessmen and Canadian confederation.
Candidate p-5139 is Andrew Michael Smith II, whose history dissertation was at Maryland in 2004.

notes: None of the eleven candidates matches. The remaining LC records identify Andrea Smith, Andrew W. M. Smith, Adam Smith, Angel Kenneth Smith, Annette M. Smith, Angela M. Smith and Alan H. Smith, with different careers or works.

who: David B. Wilson, historian of science and professor of history and philosophy at Iowa State University.

evidence.says: Iowa State's October 1997 announcement names David Wilson as the instructor of its History of Science and Religion course.
The publisher identifies David B. Wilson, author of Seeking Nature's Logic (2009), as professor of history and philosophy at Iowa State.
Candidate p-3987 is David A. Wilson, author of Paine and Cobbett and professor in Toronto's Celtic Studies Program and History Department.
Candidate p-129161 is David Mackenzie Wilson, British Museum director in 1977–1992 and Viking Age specialist.
Candidate p-148794 is David H. Wilson Jr., a Portland employment lawyer with a Wisconsin JD from 1972 and law-school teaching appointments.

notes: All three candidates are different people; the Iowa State supervisor's middle initial is B.

who: Trude Jacobsen Gidaszewski, Southeast Asian historian at Northern Illinois University, PhD Queensland 2004.

evidence.says: NIU's history profile gives a Queensland PhD in 2004, Southeast Asian teaching and research, and authorship of Lost Goddesses (2008).
The 2014 author biography identifies Trude Jacobsen as an associate professor in NIU's Department of History.
The authority for Jacobsen, Trudy explicitly includes Jacobsen, Trude as a variant and cites Lost Goddesses (2008) and a 2010 work published as Trude Jacobsen.

notes: Explicit authority-name variant, shared book and matching Queensland doctorate establish the match.

who: Historian of early United States politics and culture at Louisiana State University, PhD American history, Virginia 1994.

evidence.says: LSU identifies Burstein as Charles Phelps Manship Professor and gives his Virginia PhD in American history, 1994; research and teaching concern the early republic.
LSU's graduate student directory lists James Bishop's advisor as Professor Andrew Burstein.
The candidate authority cites The Inner Jefferson and identifies Burstein as Charles P. Manship Professor of History at LSU and author of books on early American politics and culture.

notes: The authority's LSU appointment, the Virginia doctorate and Bishop's advising record agree.

who: Joel H. Wiener, historian of nineteenth-century Britain and its press at City College, CUNY.

evidence.says: City College's History Department lists Dr. Joel Wiener among its emeritus faculty.
The publisher identifies Joel H. Wiener as professor of history at City College of New York, a specialist in nineteenth-century British history and author of The War of the Unstamped (1969).
The authority heading is Wiener, Joel H.; its identifying work is The War of the Unstamped (1969).

notes: Same CUNY historian and identifying book; the British press specialization agrees with the students' research.

who: Hal K. Rothman, historian of the American West and environmental history at UNLV from 1992.

evidence.says: UNLV Library identifies Hal Rothman as a UNLV history professor who arrived in 1992, chaired the department in 2002–2005 and wrote Neon Metropolis.
UNLV's repository lists Hal Rothman as first committee member for Gerhard Grytz's PhD dissertation on German Arizonians.
The authority explicitly connects the names Hal Rothman and Hal K. Rothman, citing Preserving Different Pasts, A Tradition of Caring and Playing the Odds.

notes: The authority's name variants and UNLV career establish the match. The repository dates Grytz's dissertation 2003, whereas the AHA entry gives 2004.

who: Robert Freeman Smith, Latin American and foreign-relations historian at Toledo from 1969, PhD Wisconsin 1958.

evidence.says: Toledo's archive identifies Robert Freeman Smith, his Wisconsin PhD in 1958, arrival at Toledo in 1969 and books on Cuba, Mexico and United States foreign relations.
A 1989 AHR contribution is by Robert Freeman Smith, University of Toledo, confirming his name and affiliation in a student's completion year.
Candidate p-3670 is Robert Courtney Smith, author of Mexican New York and affiliated with Barnard College in the authority's 1997 citation.
Candidate p-4286 is Robert W. Smith, history professor at Worcester State with a William and Mary PhD.
Candidate p-71584 is Robert J. Smith, author of The Ecole normale superieure and the Third Republic.
Candidate p-71585 is Robert Neil Smith, who completed his Georgia doctorate in 2011 and wrote An Evil Day in Georgia.
Candidate p-131966 is Robert William Smith, author of The Expanding Universe and The Hubble Revolution, with a physical-sciences museum appointment.
Candidate p-28123 identifies himself as Robert St John Smith and records an Exeter history PhD candidacy starting in 2024.

notes: None of the eleven candidates is Robert Freeman Smith. The remaining authorities identify Robert Owen, Ralph Bernard, Robert Charles, Robert Samuel and Robert Michael Smith, all distinct from the Toledo historian.

who: Historian of women and gender at UC Riverside and later Arizona State University, PhD Yale 1975.

evidence.says: A 1988 Journal of American History review identifies Sarah Stage's affiliation as the University of California, Riverside.
ASU's memorial records a Yale PhD and teaching in American Studies and Women's Studies at UC Riverside and ASU West.
ASU's faculty profile gives a Yale PhD in 1975 and identifies Stage as author of Female Complaints and co-editor of Rethinking Home Economics.
The authority identifies the author of Female Complaints and Rethinking Home Economics as Sarah Stage, cites her ASU appointment and gives a Yale PhD in 1975.

notes: The Riverside career, field, books, ASU affiliation and doctorate connect the supervisor to the candidate.
